key_insight: Physics-informed Vision Transformer frameworks estimate diffuse horizontal irradiance from scarce sky imagery with RMSE close to a full-data ViT baseline.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support photovoltaic performance optimisation and solar forecasting where irradiance instrumentation and long-term image datasets are limited.
method: Add calculated extraterrestrial irradiance and cyclic time encodings as instrument-free atmospheric features.
Predict synthetic global horizontal irradiance, then use it to refine diffuse irradiance estimation.
Process raw and overlay-enhanced fisheye images in parallel, using unsupervised, physics-informed cloud segmentation.
evidence_signal: Using Chilbolton Observatory data, single-month training and temporally disjoint full-year testing yielded RMSE within 2–3 W/m² for the sequential framework and 1–6 W/m² for the dual-parallel framework of a full-data ViT baseline.
watch_item: Validation at one temperate-climate observatory leaves transferability to other climates and sky-camera setups uncertain.
paper_title: Vision Transformers for Estimating Irradiance Using Data Scarce Sky Images
